tr_h_list: When a user submits valid credentials, the system shall authenticate the user.
When a user submits invalid credentials, the system shall not authenticate the user.
When a user submits credentials with exactly the maximum allowed number of characters, the system shall authenticate the user.
When a user requests MFA, the system shall enable multi-factor authentication.
When a user requests MFA with an invalid phone number, the system shall not enable MFA.
When a user requests MFA with a phone number that is exactly the minimum required length, the system shall enable MFA.
When a user exceeds the maximum allowed number of failed login attempts, the system shall lock the user's account.
When a user exceeds the maximum allowed number of failed login attempts with an invalid username, the system shall not lock the account.
When a user exceeds the maximum allowed number of failed login attempts with exactly the threshold number of attempts, the system shall lock the user's account.
When a token or session has expired, the system shall require re-authentication.
When a user attempts to use an expired token, the system shall not authenticate the user.
When a user attempts to use a token that is exactly at the expiration threshold, the system shall require re-authentication.
When a user attempts to set a password, the system shall reject the password if it does not contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one symbol.
When a token is generated, the system shall sign it with RS256 (asymmetric) algorithm.
When a connection is established, the system shall use TLS 1.2 or higher protocol.
When a user attempts to log in, the system shall lock the account after 5 failed login attempts.
When an account is locked, the system shall unlock it after 30 minutes.
When a session is stored, the system shall set its TTL to be aligned with the refresh token TTL.
When a password change request is received, the system shall verify that the new password meets the password requirements.
When a token is verified, the system shall check that it was signed with RS256 (asymmetric) algorithm.
When a connection is established, the system shall negotiate TLS 1.2 or higher protocol.
When a user attempts to log in, the system shall increment the failed login attempt counter.
When an account is locked, the system shall display a message indicating the remaining lock duration.
When a session is stored, the system shall set its TTL to be aligned with the refresh token TTL.
When a user attempts to log in more than 5 times with incorrect credentials, the system shall lock the account.
When an account is locked, the system shall prevent login for 30 minutes.
When a session store TTL expires, the system shall remove the associated session data.
When a user attempts to log in after account lock duration has expired, the system shall allow login.
When a user logs in successfully, the system shall reset failed login attempt counter.
When User attempts to Login, the System shall authenticate credentials.
When User attempts to Change password, the System shall update password.
When Client requests Refresh token, the System shall issue new access token.
When Rate Limiter detects excessive login attempts, the System shall lock account.
When User enables MFA, the System shall configure MFA settings.
When Request Router receives AuthRequest, the System shall route to AuthController.
When User logs out, the System shall invalidate session.
When TokenService receives token, the System shall invalidate token.
The System shall authenticate user within 2 seconds.
The System shall update password within 1 second.
The System shall issue new access token within 1 second.
The System shall lock account within 1 second of excessive login attempts.
When a user attempts to log in with an incorrect password, the system shall lock their account after exactly three failed login attempts.
The system shall validate an authentication request to ensure it conforms to the OAuth 2.0 protocol and JSON Web Token (JWT) format.
When a user requests to change their password, the system shall prompt them to enter their current and new passwords.
The system shall handle a database connection error by displaying an error message to the user within five seconds.
When a user requests an authentication token refresh within one hour of the previous refresh, the system shall refresh their authentication token.
